item.title: Fairly heavy rainfall expected in parts of the island
item.description: Showers will occur at times in the Northern, North-Central, Eastern and Central provinces, according to the Department of Meteorology. MORE..

item.title: Venezuela announces amnesty bill that could lead to mass release of political prisoners
item.description: Venezuela s acting President Delcy Rodríguez on Friday announced an amnesty bill that could lead to the release of hundreds of prisoners, including opposition leaders, journalists and human rights activists detained for political reasons. MORE..

item.title: GMOA to convene special Executive Committee meeting
item.description: The Government Medical Officers Association (GMOA) has announced that it will hold a special Executive Committee meeting today (31) to decide on future actions in relation to its unresolved issues. MORE..

item.title: UN risks imminent financial collapse , secretary general warns
item.description: The United Nations is at risk of “imminent financial collapse” due to member states not paying their fees, the body s head has warned. MORE..

item.title: Father kills teenage daughter with sharp weapon over mobile phone dispute
item.description: A 14-year-old girl was allegedly killed by her father with a sharp weapon following a dispute over a mobile phone last night (30), according to police. MORE..

item.title: More than 200 killed in coltan mine collapse in east Congo, official says
item.description: More than 200 people were killed this week in a collapse at the Rubaya coltan mine in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, Lumumba Kambere Muyisa, spokesperson for the rebel-appointed governor of the province where the mine is located, told Reuters on Friday. MORE..

item.title: Sri Lankans in Israel urged to remain vigilant amid rising tensions – Embassy
item.description: The Sri Lankan Embassy in Israel has advised Sri Lankan nationals residing in Israel to remain vigilant in light of escalating security developments across the Middle East. MORE..

item.title: President extends declaration of essential services following Cyclone Ditwah
item.description: In response to the ongoing post-disaster situation caused by Cyclone Ditwah, President Anura Kumara Dissanayake has extended the declaration of certain services as essential public services under the Essential Public Services Act, No. 61 of 1979. MORE..

item.title: Dy Minister outlines govt measures to rebuild industries affected by Cyclone Ditwah
item.description: Deputy Minister of Industry and Entrepreneurship Development Chathuranga Abeysinghe has stated that the government is taking measures to provide the necessary support to rebuild industries devastated by Cyclone Ditwah. MORE..

item.title: US government partially shuts down despite last minute funding deal
item.description: The United States federal government has partially shutdown despite a last-ditch funding deal approved by the US Senate. MORE..
